context.requirement_text: Second requirement of S7. Ports and runs, via REQ-205's harness, the four SwiftRoute scenario YAMLs. All new code is in test/. No lib/ changes, no migrations, no new routes.

task.description: Apply the REVIEWER idiom gate to REQ-206's implementation (commit 7bd75cb5). Check: (1) OTP idiom — test code using Letflow context modules correctly (no GenServer/Agent abuses in test support); (2) supervision integrity — no test code that spawns unsupervised processes or crashes supervised ones; (3) scope creep — does the implementation stay within REQ-206's stated scope (runner extension + 4 scenario YAMLs + test file)? Any new lib/ modules or public functions not in the design? (4) decision-record consistency — does the Runner extension pattern (SKIP/UNBUILT_FEATURE) contradict any decision record in docs/migration/decisions/? Verify against docs/migration/stage-7-simulation-uat-parity.md. Return PASS or FAIL with specific line references for any violations.
acceptance_criteria: OTP idiom correct in test support modules (no bare spawn, no raw send to named processes)
No scope creep beyond design §1-§4 (runner extension, scenario YAMLs, test file only)
Decision records not contradicted (no new library without a decision record if this requirement adds any to mix.exs)

result.summary: REQ-206 passes all four REVIEWER gate questions. OTP idiom: clean. Supervision: no bare spawns, correct Sandbox.mode. Scope: ScenarioFixture is explicitly within REQ-206 scope per design §1.3; no lib/ changes; no new mix.exs dependencies. Decision-record consistency: no contradictions. Three non-blocking observations filed below; none block TEST-DESIGNER.

findings.description: parse_action!/1 uses String.to_existing_atom(String.downcase(method)) to parse HTTP method atoms from scenario action strings. Correct pattern — :existing_atom, not :atom. Standard HTTP method atoms (:get, :post, etc.) are already in the atom table by the time these tests run (Plug.Test requires them). The bang suffix correctly signals a raise on malformed input. Recorded as correct-and-intentional, not a concern.

walk_path/3's list-index clause ({{produces.X.items.0.id}} style) is not explicitly named in design doc §5's template substitution spec. It is, however, a necessary consequence of the task-inbox response shape (paginated {items: [...], total: N}) — REQ-205 §6's task_assigned verification requires extracting a task_id from a list response, which the scenario YAML's produces chain must index into. This is a design-doc underspecification, not an over-build. Recommend CODE-DESIGNER retrospectively amend §5 in the design doc to name this form explicitly before REQ-207 authoring, so REQ-207's own scenario YAML authors know the syntax is available.

RunReport.step_result() and Scenario.step() are @type-spec'd plain maps with optional keys, not typed structs. This is consistent with REQ-205's original design (which established this shape). As the corpus grows through REQ-207 and REQ-208 (9 vortex, 10 meridian actors, broader step variety), a typed struct for step_result would make unrepresentable states unrepresentable earlier — e.g. a :skip result with a nil severity field is currently only caught by the ArgumentError raise in run_steps/1, not by the type system. Filing as a type-safety observation for a future requirement rather than blocking here, consistent with REVIEWER role rules.

otp_idiom.evidence: runner.ex and scenario_fixture.ex are pure functional modules — no GenServer, no bare spawn, no Process.register, no send to named processes. ScenarioFixture uses compile-time @via_atoms/@severity_atoms/@check_atoms/@method_atoms lookup maps (not String.to_atom/1 from YAML content) with fail-loud ArgumentError on unrecognized values. custom_predicate/1 uses named function-clause dispatch (idiomatic), not a data-driven map attribute. @router_opts = Letflow.Router.init([]) is a module-level constant, not a shared mutable process.

supervision_integrity.evidence: No bare spawn, no Task.async without supervision context, no unsupervised processes. Sandbox.mode(:auto) is correct for async: false tests with real Postgres tenant schema creation — prevents DB connection sharing violations across the setup/test/teardown boundary. on_exit teardown drops tenant schema (DROP SCHEMA CASCADE) and deletes identity/onboarding/tenant records via Repo.delete_all — no orphaned data. All API calls go through Letflow.Router.call/2 (Plug.Test), which is stateless and does not interact with the OTP supervision tree (no process messages sent to InstanceSupervisor or Engine processes).

scope_creep.evidence: ScenarioFixture is explicitly within REQ-206's scope: design doc §1.3 states 'REQ-206 is that scope' for the YAML→Scenario parser REQ-205 OQ-2 deferred. @simple_approval_graph inline process definition in test file is a documented workaround for SERVICE_TASK not-yet-implemented (moduledoc §2), test-only, no new lib/ module or public API. No lib/ changes. No new mix.exs dependencies (yaml_elixir was REQ-205's addition, already REVIEWER-signed). list-index template form in walk_path/3 is a necessary harness extension for task-inbox response parsing, not a forward-looking addition (R206-02 above).

decision_record_consistency.evidence: No new mix.exs dependencies. No contradiction with any docs/migration/decisions/ records. :skip via-type and :unbuilt_feature disposition are test-harness vocabulary extensions; no decision record required. Stage-7 doc (docs/migration/stage-7-simulation-uat-parity.md): implementation stays within S7's stated scope. No new library, no new architectural pattern, no conflict with any 0001–0012 decision records reviewed.
